gap_report: the three classical typologies of suffering (three sufferings, eight sufferings, pervasive-conditioning-suffering as subtlest renunciation object) and the four-noble-truths citation all come from single sources (TARAC13_TDZ three times, TARAC17_TSN once) within this batch; they are standard pan-Buddhist doctrine but no other commentary in the corpus happens to restate them here, so the drafter should attribute narrowly rather than imply corpus-wide agreement

the alternate five-paths-based reading of the bde/dge/zhi tetrad (C3) is itself reported second-hand by TARAC03_GDD as the view of unnamed 'other scholars' -- the drafter should preserve that double remove (GDD reporting an unnamed view) rather than attribute it to GDD directly

the tantric completion-stage dissolution of the suffering/bliss duality (C10) is attested only in TARAC12_PDS (the corpus's sole Nyingma source); no Sakya, Kagyu, or Gelug source in this extraction offers a comparable or contrasting tantric reading

DTG's sevenfold rebirth-scheme claim (C13) merges two passages (I-65, I-16) that count the seven differently (three lower + five higher vs. three lower + three higher + one combined desire/form); the drafter should hedge on the exact sevenfold breakdown rather than state one fixed list

extraction was deliberately selective given how pervasively སྡུག་བསྔལ appears in generic benefit-catalogue prose across all 16 commentaries (poverty, illness, spirits, curses, etc.); only passages that explain or classify the term itself were kept, per the drafting brief -- a separate 'benefits' pass on this corpus could surface much more such material if wanted
